name: Moving Average Regime
rationale: Moving-average regime rules use market state as a filter rather than a standalone return-maximizing prediction.
expected_benefit: Potentially lower drawdowns and clearer exposure control during sustained declines.
failure_modes: May duplicate prior trend-following failures if the hypothesis is not materially different.

canonical_variants.name: EMA 50 regime filter
canonical_variants.description: Hold only when close is above a 50-day EMA.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A 50-day EMA regime filter may react faster than a 200-day SMA and improve drawdown-adjusted performance without excessive turnover.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative while retaining at least 75% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: EMA/SMA confirmation regime
canonical_variants.description: Require close above a medium EMA and a long SMA before holding risk.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A dual moving-average confirmation rule may reduce false positives versus a single trend filter.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe while retaining at least 70% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: EMA plus RSI trend confirmation
canonical_variants.description: Hold only when price is above an EMA and RSI confirms positive momentum.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: Combining a price regime filter with RSI momentum confirmation may avoid weak trend entries.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe and avoid worse max drawdown than buy-and-hold.

suggested_validation: Write why this is not merely repeating the prior long/cash trend test.
Use one prespecified filter before trying a sweep.
references: Faber, A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
Practitioner research on moving-average regime filters
execution_notes: Executable when variants use same-symbol SMA, EMA, RSI, and long/cash rules.
